title: When the water moves but the clock doesn't
question: Can a closed-form water-transfer model keep stored water, stored time and receipts consistent at numerical limits?
method: An explicit two-compartment linear passive-water hypothesis, finite-domain event handling, immutable state, snapshot continuation and 16 recorded synthetic tests; preserve the independent precision counterexamples and their corrections.
finding: The retained final implementation refuses unsupported clock, transfer and boundary-time representations, reports stored endpoint transfer, and stops at the declared domain. Its October 9 record reports final independent and Counsel acceptance within numerical scope.
claim_scope: The unchanged, uncalibrated Python numerical artifact and its 16 historically completed synthetic checks; not a biological hydration trajectory, germination result or proof for all floating-point inputs.
limitations: Constant conductance, linear storage and persistent contact are provisional, uncalibrated assumptions.
No measured lotus parameter set, metabolism, viability diagnosis, growth or germination is implemented.
Floating-point endpoint rounding remains; split-duration continuation is only within roundoff.
Historical checks are reused, not rerun during exhibit preparation.
open_questions: What observations and constitutive hypothesis would justify a biological continuation?
How should conductance and storage be independently identified, given that uptake alone cannot identify both?
